title: How a CIMD client is trusted
lede: The client's identifier is a URL it controls; Privilege fetches the JSON document there and the admin decides which URLs to trust.

nodes.label: Client identifier is an https URL

edges.label: accepted: client is known, no secret

steps.title: The identity is a URL
steps.what: A client's identifier is an https URL its owner controls; the document there must name that same URL.
steps.why: The identifier must equal the URL it was fetched from, or the document is not valid.

steps.title: Privilege reads the document
steps.what: The document describes the client: name, redirect URIs, grant types, response types and token endpoint auth none.
steps.why: Public clients use PKCE and hold no secret to steal.

steps.title: The admin decides which URLs to trust
steps.what: The MCP Client Documents settings hold the accepted document URLs, with a type, a fetch status and a gateway cache period (documented default 24 hours).
steps.why: An empty list leaves the feature off and dynamic registration continues as before.
